A.explanation: Current is not zero because the three e.m.f.s do not cancel - two cells drive current one way and only one opposes.

B.explanation: Net e.m.f. $E$ drives current $I = E/3R$, so $V = IR = E/3$ across each resistor $R$.

C.explanation: This would need net e.m.f. $2E$, but the opposing cell reduces the total to $E$, not $2E$.

D.explanation: This is the full cell e.m.f. $E$, but it is shared equally between three identical series resistors.

hints: Notice the circuit is a single closed loop with three resistors $R$ in series, so the same current $I$ flows through each resistor.
Check the polarity of the three cells $E$ around the loop - two push current in the same clockwise sense and the third pushes the opposite way.
Combine the e.m.f.s to find the net e.m.f. driving the loop, then use $V = IR$ with total resistance $3R$ to find the share across one $R$.
walkthrough: Identify the loop: the three resistors $R$ are in series, so total resistance is $R + R + R = 3R$ and one common current $I$ flows.
Find the net e.m.f. using Kirchhoff's second law. Going round the loop, two cells of e.m.f. $E$ act in one direction and one cell $E$ acts in the opposite direction.
Net e.m.f. $= E + E - E = E$. Internal resistance is negligible, so this whole e.m.f. drives current through the external resistors.
Current in loop is $I = \text{net e.m.f.} / \text{total resistance} = E/(3R)$.
Potential difference across one resistor is $V = IR = [E/(3R)] \times R = E/3$.
